items.stem: Define the term 'operations management'.
items.answer: The management of the process that transforms inputs into outputs (goods and services) efficiently and to the required quality.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition – The management of the process that transforms inputs into outputs (goods and services) efficiently and to the required quality. 1 mark: partial definition or a relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain how operations management adds value.
items.answer: It organises inputs efficiently and transforms them into products of the right quality that customers will pay more for than the cost of the inputs.
items.markingKey: 1 mark efficient transformation; 1 mark quality/customer value; 1 mark price exceeds input cost. [3]

items.stem: Explain the transformation process for a service business such as a restaurant.
items.answer: Inputs such as food, staff, equipment and premises are transformed through cooking and serving into outputs of meals and a dining experience for customers.
items.markingKey: 1 mark inputs; 1 mark process; 1 mark outputs. [3]

items.stem: Hamid Engineering Ltd is a private limited company based in Lahore, Pakistan. It makes pumps and valves for farms and factories and employs about 150 people. Its factory is working at full capacity and some orders are delivered late. Explain how better operations management could add value at Hamid Engineering.
items.answer: Points to develop for Hamid Engineering: operations management controls the transformation process; less waste lowers costs; better quality raises the price customers pay; faster delivery improves customer service.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: operations management controls the transformation process. AO2 Application [1]: point linked to Hamid Engineering (engineering). AO3 Analysis [1]: developed explanation of the consequence, e.g. less waste lowers costs; better quality raises the price customers pay. [3]

items.stem: Based in Alexandria, Atlas Furniture plc (public limited company) makes furniture and sells it through 40 stores. The business has around 1,300 employees. Sales in its stores have fallen while online sales have grown. Explain the inputs, processes and outputs in the operations of Atlas Furniture.
items.answer: Points to develop for Atlas Furniture: operations transform inputs into outputs; inputs such as labour, materials and equipment; processes that add value to furniture; outputs sold to customers.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: operations transform inputs into outputs. AO2 Application [1]: point linked to Atlas Furniture (furniture manufacturing and retail). AO3 Analysis [1]: developed explanation of the consequence, e.g. inputs such as labour, materials and equipment; processes that add value to furniture. [3]

items.answer: For: efficiency lowers costs; quality builds reputation; reliable delivery. Against: marketing and finance also essential; external factors; depends on the industry. Judgement: for Green Valley Dairy it depends mainly on the competitive position, and also on the type of product.

items.answer: Flour

Identify and explain one advantage for Andina Solar of investing in new technology in its transformation process.
items.answer: Higher productivity; this would help Andina Solar, which designs and installs solar power systems for farms, mines and homes.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: relevant advantage, e.g. higher productivity; consistent quality; lower unit costs. 1 mark: explained in the context of Andina Solar (renewable energy). [2]

items.stem: Define the term 'labour productivity'.
items.answer: The output per worker in a given period: total output ÷ number of workers.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition – The output per worker in a given period: total output ÷ number of workers. 1 mark: partial definition or a relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain the difference between efficiency and effectiveness.
items.answer: Efficiency means using as few resources as possible to produce output; effectiveness means achieving the objectives, such as producing what customers want. A business can be efficient without being effective.
items.markingKey: 1 mark efficiency; 1 mark effectiveness; 1 mark contrast/example. [3]

items.stem: Explain why higher labour productivity may not lead to lower unit costs.
items.answer: If productivity rises because of higher wages or expensive new machinery, the extra costs may outweigh the gain in output per worker.
items.markingKey: 1 mark higher costs; 1 mark comparison with output gain. [2]

items.stem: Labour turnover among machinists has risen sharply this year. Tanvir Textiles Ltd, a private limited company in Bangladesh with about 420 employees, makes shirts and T-shirts for European fashion retailers. Explain the benefits to Tanvir Textiles of improving efficiency.
items.answer: Points to develop for Tanvir Textiles: efficiency means minimum resource use; lower unit costs; more competitive prices or higher margins; less waste benefits the environment.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: efficiency means minimum resource use. AO2 Application [1]: point linked to Tanvir Textiles (clothing manufacturing). AO3 Analysis [1]: developed explanation of the consequence, e.g. lower unit costs; more competitive prices or higher margins. [3]

items.answer: Points to develop for Café Cordillera: labour productivity is output per worker; training improves skills; investment in technology; motivation and better working methods.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: labour productivity is output per worker. AO2 Application [1]: point linked to Café Cordillera (food and drink retail). AO3 Analysis [1]: developed explanation of the consequence, e.g. training improves skills; investment in technology. [3]

items.stem: Define the term 'job production'.
items.answer: Producing a single, one-off product to the customer's individual requirements.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition – Producing a single, one-off product to the customer's individual requirements. 1 mark: partial definition or a relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage of batch production.
items.answer: Advantage: it allows some variety while keeping unit costs lower than job production. Disadvantage: time is lost and costs rise when machines are reset between batches, and inventory of each batch must be stored.
items.markingKey: 1 mark advantage, 1 mark explanation; 1 mark disadvantage, 1 mark explanation. [4]

items.stem: Explain why flow production may lead to low worker motivation.
items.answer: Workers repeat the same simple task on the production line, which is boring and gives little responsibility or sense of achievement.
items.markingKey: 1 mark repetitive tasks; 1 mark link to motivation. [2]

items.answer: Production that uses a high proportion of labour compared with capital.

items.stem: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage of capital-intensive production.
items.answer: Advantage: machines produce large volumes at consistent quality and low unit cost. Disadvantage: the initial investment is very high and machine breakdowns can stop production.
items.markingKey: 1 mark advantage, 1 mark explanation; 1 mark disadvantage, 1 mark explanation. [4]

items.stem: Explain two factors that influence whether a business chooses labour-intensive or capital-intensive production.
items.answer: The relative cost of labour and capital; and the scale of production – large-scale production justifies investment in machinery.
items.markingKey: 2 × (1 mark factor, 1 mark explanation): relative costs, scale, product type, finance, skills available. [4]

items.stem: Explain how mass customisation combines features of job and flow production.
items.answer: Flexible computer-controlled machines produce in large volumes like flow production, but each product can be tailored to the customer like job production.
items.markingKey: 1 mark high volume/low cost; 1 mark individual tailoring. [2]

items.stem: Petra Prints is a private limited company in Amman, Jordan with about 35 staff. It prints leaflets, posters and packaging for local businesses. A large customer has started to pay its invoices late. Explain the effects on Petra Prints of changing from job production to batch production.
items.answer: Points to develop for Petra Prints: job production makes one-off products; batch production lowers unit costs; less individual choice for customers; need for inventory and machine set-up.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: job production makes one-off products. AO2 Application [1]: point linked to Petra Prints (printing). AO3 Analysis [1]: developed explanation of the consequence, e.g. batch production lowers unit costs; less individual choice for customers. [3]

items.stem: Gold Coast Cocoa Ltd is a private limited company based in Accra, Ghana. It buys cocoa from local co-operatives and makes premium chocolate bars and employs about 450 people. World cocoa prices have doubled in eighteen months. (a) Explain one advantage to Gold Coast Cocoa of introducing mass customisation. (b) Evaluate whether Gold Coast Cocoa should change to flow production.
items.answer: (a) Meets individual customer needs. (b) For: lower unit costs; higher output; consistent quality. Against: high investment; inflexible; demand may be too small. Judgement: for Gold Coast Cocoa it depends mainly on the size and stability of demand, and also on the finance available.

AO4 Evaluation [4]: a justified judgement that weighs the arguments, e.g. it depends on the size and stability of demand; the finance available; customer need for variety. A top-level answer reaches a supported conclusion specific to Gold Coast Cocoa. [12]

items.stem: Andina Solar is a private limited company in Santiago, Chile with about 380 staff. It designs and installs solar power systems for farms, mines and homes.
